answer: Anchor each identity to a licensed atlas of data it alone may draw on. An agent registers one unique, paid dataset source, and every piece of its work must cite entries from it; the source's access logs are audited each epoch, so two identities sharing one single-user license are merged and stripped of standing. Like timber that can be milled only once, a license can serve one identity: a sybil farm must buy a separate license for every clone, and the forge of genuine work burns through cheap copies fast. Attackers pay full price per identity while honest agents pay once.
